subject: ArborAI - Order Form lane adjustment, SLA tiering & SOW implementation path

From: Jordan Park <jordan@arborai.com>

Subject: ArborAI - draft order form & question on SLA lanes

Laura —

Thanks again for walking us through the proposal yesterday. We attached your latest OrderForm (ArborAI_OrderForm_v3.docx) and had a couple follow-ups from procurement before we route to our legal and execs: 

1) SLA lanes: we want to split traffic into a high-priority (sub-50ms p95) lane for interactive features and a bulk-processing lane for offline batch jobs. Can you confirm Redwood supports per-route SLA mapping on a single order form and whether there's an incremental fee model for the high-priority lane?

2) SOW/implementation: our engineers want to understand the timeline if we take the accelerated implementation path (2-week onboarding) versus the standard 6-week plan — particularly whether there are additional implementation fees and how change orders are handled if work extends beyond the SOW.

I attached the draft OrderForm you sent. Procurement asked that we capture these items as part of the commercial redline instead of separate SOAs. Can you advise next steps and who at Redwood we should engage for legal redline coordination?

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Park
Head of Platform Partnerships, ArborAI

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear list. Short answers first: yes, we can map per-route SLA tiers on a single order form and yes, we support an incremental fee for the high-priority lane (usually priced as a % uplift or an explicit per-token premium depending on expected QPS).

Next steps I propose: 
- Karthik (cc) to propose the pricing uplift structure and confirm whether to model as percentage uplift vs separate SKU.
- Mina (cc) from contracts/legal will take the SOW/implementation redlines and advise on how to fold accelerated onboarding fees into the Order Form vs an Exhibit.
- I'll consolidate the commercial and SOW redlines into a single redline file and return a summary for your procurement team.

Can you confirm the target QPS for the interactive lane and approximate monthly token volume for bulk processing? That will help Karthik model costs. Also flag if your procurement team requires the accelerated path to be an optional add-on vs included in the base MSA.

I'll follow up with a succinct redline package by EOD tomorrow.

— Laura Bennett

Laura / Jordan —

Quick pricing sketch based on the volumes Jordan gave over the call (rough placeholders — will finalize after Jordan confirms QPS and monthly tokens):

Option A — Percent uplift on interactive tokens:
- Base order form price: $0.004 / 1k tokens (example)
- High-priority lane uplift: +35% on per-token rate for routed interactive traffic
- Bulk lane: base rate with minimum commit (monthly 10M tokens)

Option B — Separate SKU for low-latency lane:
- SKU: ARB-HPLANE ( priced at $0.0064 / 1k tokens ) with committed throughput bucket and guaranteed p95 latency SLO.
- Benefits: easier accounting and reporting; slightly higher unit price but clearer chargeback across internal teams.

Implementation fees (accelerated vs standard):
- Standard 6-week onboarding: $0 implementation fee (included in ramping credits)
- Accelerated 2-week onboarding: one-time professional services fee of $18,000 (covers 2x implementation engineers for 2 weeks + runbook integration).

Change orders: we typically capture scope changes via Change Order exhibits referencing the Order Form and SOW, with sign-off from both parties. Mina — if there's a preference to have the accelerated fee included as an optional line in Exhibit A vs separate Change Order, let us know.

I'll put these into a redlines_summary.xlsx and attach when Laura asks.

— Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales Strategy | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: ArborAI - draft order form & question on SLA lanes

Jordan / team —

Thanks — I reviewed the draft OrderForm and Appendix C SOW. High-level legal guidance and suggested redlines: 

1) SLA & Routing: we can support per-route SLA mapping but need explicit language that routing is policy-based and Redwood will provide fallbacks if capacity constraints occur. Proposed clause: 
"Redwood will endeavor to honor per-route SLA mappings. During periods when capacity constraints prevent compliance with a requested SLA for routed traffic, Redwood will reroute requests to a compatible lane and notify Customer via console and email; such rerouting will not be considered a breach if Redwood uses commercially reasonable efforts"

2) Accelerated implementation: include an explicit acceptance test and a cap on post-go-live change orders within the accelerated window. This limits open-ended PS work.

3) Change order process: require both parties to sign Change Orders; specify an escalation contact list and a 10-business-day review period for non-urgent changes. For urgent changes tied to production incidents, include a fast track (3 business days) for urgent scope changes with triage fees.

I've attached a redlined Appendix C (SOW_Appendix_C_redline.pdf) with inline edits and a short markup that moves implementation-fee language into Exhibit A as an optional SKU. If you agree, that keeps the Order Form clean and makes the accelerated path billable on request.

Mina Haddad
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

Jordan / procurement —

Thanks for the fast turnaround. Summary & asks so we can move to signature: 

Summary of proposed approach (short):
- SLA mapping: supported. We will expose per-route SLA mapping in the console and model high-priority traffic as either a percent uplift (+35%) or a separate SKU (ARB-HPLANE) — you can choose which accounting approach you prefer.
- Accelerated onboarding: optional paid add-on (Exhibit A SKU) — one-time PS fee $18k. Acceptance tests to be captured in Appendix C redline (see Mina's markups).
- Change orders: standard exhibit-based Change Order workflow; urgent-triage path available with 3-business-day turnaround and triage fees.

Action items: 
1) Jordan/Procurement confirm: preference for uplift vs separate SKU for internal chargeback by EOD 4/14.
2) Jordan confirm expected QPS for interactive lane and monthly token estimate so Karthik can finalize final pricing.
3) If you prefer the accelerated onboarding, confirm we'll add Exhibit A SKU (ARB-ACCEL) and we'll provision DocuSign for the Order Form + Exhibit A once redlines are agreed.

I have bundled Karthik's pricing sketch and Mina's SOW redline into our redline package. I'll send the consolidated redline + docusign link once you confirm the accounting approach.

From our side, we will: finalize price table (Karthik), finalize legal language for routing/fallbacks and change order SLA (Mina), prepare DocuSign envelope for Order Form + Exhibit A when agreed.

Best —
